reason: The cited evidence shows that Cr addition increases coercivity in related alloys (E3) and that nanoscale FM/AFM microstructures form (E1, E3), but none of the passages demonstrate exchange bias in FeCoNiCr, nor do they provide data on controlled precipitate formation or coercivity relative to FeCoNiPd/Pt baselines. Key mechanistic and comparative premises are therefore unsupported.
premises: Cr substitution into FeCoNi forms antiferromagnetic Cr-rich regions that create FM/AFM interfaces
FM/AFM interfaces produce exchange bias that pins domain walls and increases coercivity
Nanoscale Cr-rich precipitates can be controlled by heat treatment to avoid excessive loss of saturation magnetization
FeCoNiPd and FeCoNiPt are soft ferromagnets with low coercivity, serving as a valid baseline
Equiatomic FeCoNiCr can retain high saturation magnetization relative to the baseline
